sprint_note: Review page: day-based five-metric summary (Recalls/Unique/First/Due/New) replacing the session-based Current/Upcoming block; trimmed interval-forecast row; removed redundant 'Review' caption. Essay reader: new per-sentence 'difficult'/'thumbs up' feedback (new backend/sentences.py splitter, new backend/routers/sentence_feedback.py, new essaycards.sentence_feedback table). Stats page: day-based stacked Repeat/Unique/First activity chart with daily recall-rate labels (new local chart component), and a day/week/month Observed Recall selector.

files.role: The single canonical sentence-split function for essay section body_markdown. Pure function, no I/O, no DB access. Shared verbatim by backend/routers/sentence_feedback.py's three endpoints (sentences list, feedback write-time validation) — see 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 5 for the exact algorithm, which this module's docstring must restate verbatim (StoryReader backend/paragraphs.py convention).

methods.name: split_sentences
methods.purpose: Splits raw section body_markdown into an ordered list of sentence-fragment strings, preserving inline markdown syntax verbatim inside each fragment (NOT stripped — contrast StoryReader's split_paragraphs). See 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 5 for the exact normalize/fence-drop/join/regex-split algorithm.

private_objects.name: _FENCE_RE
private_objects.purpose: ^```.*$ — matches a fenced-code delimiter line, dropped entirely along with its content lines. Same pattern as StoryReader paragraphs.py's _FENCE_RE.

private_objects.name: _SENTENCE_BOUNDARY_RE
private_objects.purpose: (?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z0-9"'(\[]) — the sentence-boundary split regex per internal_flow step 5.

private_objects.name: list_essay_sentences
private_objects.purpose: GET /essays/{essay_id}/sentences handler. For each essay_sections row (essay_id=path param, order by order_index asc), calls backend.sentences.split_sentences(body_markdown) and emits one {section_id, sentence_index, text} row per sentence. 404 NOT_FOUND if essay_id does not exist.

private_objects.name: list_essay_sentence_feedback
private_objects.purpose: GET /essays/{essay_id}/sentence-feedback handler. Selects essaycards.sentence_feedback rows joined to essay_sections (essay_id=path param), ordered (section order_index asc, sentence_index asc). No re-validation against current content (10_architecture.json contracts.invariants). 404 NOT_FOUND if essay_id does not exist.

private_objects.name: update_sentence_feedback
private_objects.purpose: PATCH /sections/{section_id}/sentence-feedback handler. Loads the section (404 if missing); recomputes split_sentences(section.body_markdown); validates sentence_index in range and sentence_text matches exactly (VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise); reads the current essaycards.sentence_feedback row if any; computes the new (is_difficult, is_thumbs_up) pair per body.flag/body.value, leaving the other flag unchanged; upserts if at least one flag is true, else DELETEs; returns {section_id, sentence_index, is_difficult, is_thumbs_up} status 200. See 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 7.

private_objects.name: SectionSentences
private_objects.purpose: [NEW] Props: {section: EssaySection; sentences: SentenceRow[]; feedbackByIndex: Record<number, SentenceFeedbackRow>; onToggle: (sentenceIndex: number, text: string, flag: 'difficult' | 'thumbs_up', value: boolean) => void}. Renders each sentence as a tappable <span data-sentence-index> wrapping a <ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[[remarkNuggetRefs, ...]]} urlTransform={nuggetAwareUrlTransform} components={{a: NuggetLink...}}> instance (identical props to the whole-section render it replaces) followed by trailing ⚠/👍 indicator icons when feedbackByIndex has an entry. Tapping a sentence opens SentenceFeedbackPopover positioned below it. CLICK PRECEDENCE (binding, 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 8): the `components={{a: ...}}` anchor renderer used inside this instance's ReactMarkdown (covering both NuggetLink-resolved nugget refs and plain markdown links) must call `event.stopPropagation()` in its onClick before any navigation/overlay-open logic, so a tap on a link or nugget-ref inside a sentence is swallowed before it reaches the sentence span's own onClick — the span's tap-to-open-popover handler never fires for those taps.

private_objects.name: SentenceFeedbackPopover
private_objects.purpose: [NEW] Props: {sentenceIndex: number; rect: DOMRect; current: SentenceFeedbackRow | undefined; onToggle: (flag: 'difficult' | 'thumbs_up', value: boolean) => void; onClose: () => void}. Fixed-position below `rect` (same positioning convention as StoryReader's ReactionPopover — top: rect.bottom + 8), two independently-toggleable buttons (Difficult, Thumbs up), pressed state from `current`. Closes on tap-elsewhere or re-tap of the open sentence (does NOT auto-close on a flag toggle). Not itself part of the click-precedence rule (that rule governs SectionSentences' nested anchors vs. its own sentence-span tap, see SectionSentences entry above) — included here only because it is the popover opened by that tap.
